Messages.Author: Sydnelson
Messages.Body:
Hi, today a player ask me if is legal use deflection or telepathic misdirection to redirect the target of bleed to itself just to cycle hand in head to head game. It's possible?

Ex.: 2 players in a game. Player A, bleed, player B decline to block and play deflection choosing himself as a new target of bleed since there is no more valid targets to choose.

Deflection, Reaction, 1 blood, Dominate
[dom] Only usable when you are being bled, after blocks are declined. Tap this reacting vampire. Choose another Methuselah other than the controller of the acting minion. The acting minion is now bleeding that Methuselah.
[DOM] As above, but do not tap this vampire.

Telepathic Misdirection, Reaction, 1 blood
[aus] +1 intercept.
[AUS] Only usable when a minion is bleeding you, after blocks are declined. Tap this reacting vampire. Choose another Methuselah other than the acting minion's controller. The acting minion is now bleeding that Methuselah.

Fernando Cesar - Sydnelson

Messages.Author: Ohlmann
Messages.Body:
> Sydnelson wrote:
> Both cards says ANOTHER Methuselah other than the ACTING minion's controller. Not reacting minion controler (who plays the Deflection / Telephatic)
>
You link together two part that should not be linked. There is two conditions :
* redirect to ANOTHER methuselah
* that another methuselah cannot be the one of the acting minion.

If you were right, it would be written :
>
> Choose a Methuselah other than the acting minion's controller
>
Like it is written on superior Blissful Agony :

> Strike: combat ends. Choose a minion controlled by a Methuselah other than the opposing vampire's controller. The opposing vampire enters combat with that minion.
>
Note that you can choose one of your own vampire with Blissful agony, while you cannot redirect to yourself with Deflection.

Messages.Author: Kiddo
Messages.Body:
However, in a game with only 2 players left, you can redirect a bleed to yourself via My Enemy's Enemy, just in order to cycle a card.

That is possible due to a)you being your predator's predator in a 2-player game and b)this card, unlike others, doesn't specify that the new target cannot be an originally targeted player...

> My Enemy's Enemy
> Type: Reaction
> Requires: Auspex
> [aus] +1 intercept.
> [AUS] Only usable when a minion controlled by your predator is bleeding you, after blocks are declined. Tap this reacting vampire. The acting minion is now bleeding your predator's predator.
>

Messages.Author: Lönkka
Messages.Body:
> Sydnelson wrote:
> I prety now that is not possible do that, I just don't know how to explain it to player but now I can see.
>
James' answer is pretty explicit, but I'll give another shot in explaining the sentence "Choose another Methuselah other than the controller of the acting minion." to the player.

"Choose another Methuselah" = Choose a Methuselah that is not YOU...

"other than the controller of the acting minion." = ...and the someone else can't be the Methuselah whose minion is bleeding.

I've underlined the key word.
So you HAVE TO choose another Methuselah which means you can't choose yourself.

So in two player situations Defections are dead cards in your hand.

Finnish  Politics!

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
Correct answers from Ohlman, jamesatzephyr and Lönkka.

About Kiddo's comment:
Yes, My Enemy's Enemy is playable in duel, but since it is played after block attemps are declined (as all other bleed redirection cards), and since the target of the action doesn't change (which is what enables new block attempts declarations), if you play it in a duel, you don't get a new chance to declare block attempts.
